findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification
findings.body: In the credentials authorize callback, the password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch at line 131 is entered whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present, even if a non-empty `totpCode` is also supplied. An attacker can send credentials containing any non-empty `totpCode` and a valid backup code; the password check is skipped and the backup code alone authenticates. This turns a backup code into a single-factor credential and allows login without the account password.

findings.title: Backup-code single-use guarantee is not atomic
findings.body: After matching a backup code, the code is invalidated by decrypting the stored array, setting the matched entry to null, and writing it back with a separate `prisma.user.update`. This read-modify-write is not transactional or protected against concurrent updates. Two simultaneous login attempts using the same backup code can both read it as unused and both succeed. Concurrent uses of different codes can also overwrite each other's updates and resurrect a previously used code.

findings.title: Dialog can be dismissed after enabling 2FA without notifying parent or resetting state
findings.body: After TOTP verification succeeds, the modal switches to the backup-code screen, but `onEnable` and `resetState` are only invoked by the explicit Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog through `onOpenChange` (for example via backdrop click, close icon, or Escape), the parent is not notified that 2FA has been enabled and the modal state is not reset. The settings UI can remain stale until a reload, and sensitive state such as backup codes or object URLs may persist.

findings.title: Backup-code matching is case- and whitespace-sensitive
findings.body: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex strings, but during login they are compared with `indexOf` after only removing dashes. The value is not trimmed or lowercased. A user who enters a valid code in uppercase, which is suggested by the UI placeholder, or with surrounding whitespace will be rejected despite having a valid backup code.

findings.title: Disable endpoint rejects uppercase backup codes
findings.body: The disable endpoint compares the supplied backup code after removing dashes but without trimming or lowercasing it. Since generated codes are lowercase hex, a valid backup code entered in uppercase or with surrounding whitespace is rejected, preventing a user from disabling 2FA with a valid code.

findings.title: No tests cover actual backup-code authentication or single-use behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a security-critical backup-code login and disable flow, but the e2e tests only verify that backup codes can be downloaded, copied, and closed. There is no test that logs in with a backup code, disables 2FA with a backup code, or asserts that a consumed backup code cannot be reused, so the core feature and its single-use guarantee are untested.
